dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: What? Don't disturb me. I'm thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm thinking about something very important!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: Have you seen that thing they call the Dainichi Mikoshi?

dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: The tallest thing in the whole country.

dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: I was thinking about how I can build something even taller than that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it's only so tall so that it can light up Byakuyakoku, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the reason for your building being so tall?

dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: To display my glory, of course! The glory of Rikoru the Great!

dialogues.speaker: Rikoru
dialogues.text: That'll show that old man Aberaku who's boss!

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: Of course. He built the Dainichi Mikoshi and saved Byakuyakoku. I used to look up to him...

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: But as it turned out, he had designs on the throne. If it wasn't for those adults, I would be dead right now.

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: That's why I will build something taller than the Dainichi Mikoshi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—How long will that take?

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: Like I care!

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: The people of Byakuyakoku should be happy that I would ask them to build such a historical wonder for me!

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: Alright, then! Stop bothering me!

response.speaker: Rikoru
response.text: Let me think. If the beams are this long... If we do it that way, the load-bearing and wood joinery...

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: Hmm? I've never seen people dressed like you are before.

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: Are you someone who fell from... that, uh, from beyond the skies?

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: So! The world does not end with our glorious nation! Well, then. Surrender your maps to me for my perusal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You give him your map...)

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: Ah, how very intricate. Not only are the landforms accurately drawn, but even the paths of the mountains and rivers can be seen.

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: Well, then. How large is this nation you call "Teyvat"? How does it measure up to Byakuyakoku?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Teyvat's a whole continent...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, Enkanomiya... That is, Byakuyakoku, is this small patch on the south end of the map.

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: Nonsense! Our lands are vast and broad! How can they occupy but such a puny space?

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: This map may seem exquisitely drawn, but is in truth an errant fraud. Away, away with it!

dialogues.speaker: Isumenasu
dialogues.text: To think I had even a moment of admiration for this cheap charlatanry, to the defilement of mine eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, suit yourself, kiddo!

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: Travelers from distant lands... *cough* You seem quite tired.

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: That won't do, you know? Many illnesses have their humble beginnings in exhaustion.

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: You must ensure that you get enough rest every day, so that you— *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: *cough* *cough* —can grow healthily.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know what, you're not looking too good yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: Ahaha, it is an old malady of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: You must maintain a healthy body to stimulate a healthy soul, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only I had more time. I would become the greatest physician in the world...

dialogues.speaker: Surepio
dialogues.text: That way, even with this body of mine, I would surely be able to walk out of my room in good health and play to my heart's content.

dialogues.speaker: Risutaiosu
dialogues.text: Stop moving!

dialogues.speaker: Risutaiosu
dialogues.text: Oh, stop it! Stop, I say! Come on, I told you to stop moving! Didn't you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon can't just stop moving...

choices.text: Imagine asking Paimon not to move...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way!

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: Ugh, alright, turn around then. I have never seen these clothes in my life.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: They're not entirely aesthetically pleasing, but they are somewhat interesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you don't like 'em, why'd you even look?

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: Seriously? Asking those lady retainers to model for me was hardly this difficult.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: That said, I've gotten quite sick of looking at the way our people dress.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: As for what you're wearing, now that's new.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: Hmm, I know. So that's how they put those clothes together... Wow, you outsiders really are shameless.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: I see, I see... So if the clothes are made like that, then the body shape should be like... this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you doing?

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: Making a statue. I mix clay and water, and then I knead them into shape with both hands. It helps to calm me — it's one of the only things that does.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: And you know what definitely doesn't calm me? Sitting in regular meetings, reading aloud based on material pre-written by those adults.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: Well, whatever. I'm done with your forms as well.

response.speaker: Risutaiosu
response.text: Now stop bothering me. Go do your own stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: Oh ho, Traveler, you look pretty interesting. What say I take a stab at reading your fortune?

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: I am Ion, after all. I never miss a reading.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sound like a hustler.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Also, Paimon remembers that his tombstone read...)

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: Oh, come now, what's with that suspicious look? I always read peoples' fortunes.

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: That said... Few of Byakuyakoku's people have happy fates awaiting them.

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: So I often cheat them, telling them that their luck will turn.

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: If nothing else, I think that I can grant them a little happiness that way.

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: In the end, they said that I couldn't tell fortunes at all. Ah, how saddening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that how it is?

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: Well, little one, I'll prove it to you, right now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—Oh? Sure! Try Paimon on for size!

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: Hmm, alright... Let me have a careful go at this... Huh. Why's there so much interference?

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: Eh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: I... can't read your fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: How could that be? I don't get it exactly right most of the time, but I usually don't fail to get a reading at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess you ain't that good, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ion
dialogues.text: It does seem so. It seems that I must continue my studies in earnest.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: Oh ho! Judging by your appearance, you must be a traveler from another nation!

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: Where do you hail from?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're from Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You describe the Mondstadt's scenery to Piramumon in a simple manner...

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: I've never heard of such a city. To think that there was such a place...

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: Hahaha! It's just as I said, then! The world couldn't possibly only be the size of Byakuyakoku!

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: I mean, if Byakuyakoku were all there was in the world, that would be a most lonely world indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: The ancient texts also talk about times before our nation was founded. That's when I began to believe that there were lands beyond ours.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: But I was still scared, you know? Scared that there was really nothing else out there.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: You have no idea, Traveler, how much your arrival sets my heart at ease. Haha, so there are many more fascinating places to see in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: It's just a shame that I have this festival called the Rite of Solar Return to attend to.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: How about this, Traveler? Tell me how you came here.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: Once the festival has ended, I'll find an opportunity to sneak out of the Dainichi Mikoshi.

dialogues.speaker: Piramumon
dialogues.text: Let's have some fruit juice together instead! Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: *sigh* So you are the traveler from afar...

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: What are you pursuing? The sight of you coming this way was grievous to watch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grief? What's there to be sad about?

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: For a singer of songs, everything in this world is worth grieving.

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: Where there are meetings, there must be partings, and those who are born will one day return to the earth...

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: Reunions are too brief to salve the pain of long separations... And as for you, Traveler...

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: Only those in pursuit of something will journey into another realm as you do.

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: The locals, who have lived here for a long time, would find such a journey romantic, but for the wayfarer themselves, it may mean unspeakable pain.

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: If you came in an earlier clime, I might have sung for you.

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: But I have sworn an oath with someone that I shall not sing again until I hear her voice.

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: I can only wish you well, though you seem far older than I...

dialogues.speaker: Orupeusu
dialogues.text: I hope your wish comes true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems like each of the Sunchildren is pretty different, huh...
